title: Faster scrolling with several spreadsheets
summary: Spreadsheets near the screen now appear as a light preview and become fully editable the moment you click them.
details: Only the table you click gets the full editor, so scrolling past many tables stays smooth.
The preview matches the editor's look, column widths and row heights, so nothing jumps when you click.
The cell you clicked is selected straight away, and the table you are editing stays live while you scroll.
imageAlt: A spreadsheet shown as a preview before clicking, and as the live editor after

title: Tab and Shift+Tab indent several list lines at once
summary: Select multiple bullet or numbered lines and press Tab to indent them all, or Shift+Tab to outdent them.
details: Works for bullet lists, numbered lists and several selected paragraphs.
Nested lists move one level per press.
imageAlt: Three selected bullet lines being indented together

title: Version history for templates
summary: See every saved version of a template, compare revisions, and restore an older one without losing the current one.
details: The history opens in a popup on the edit page.
Restoring a version makes it current and keeps the other versions.
Each version has its own edit history that you can restore individually.

title: Insert a spreadsheet of any size, and handier tools in view mode
summary: Drag across a grid to choose the size, like Insert table. View mode now has copy-table and auto-fit buttons.
details: Spreadsheet is also in the classic Insert menu.
Copy the whole table in one click, and auto-fit rows or columns to their content.
Row heights now grow when a narrower column needs more wrapped lines.
imageAlt: The drag-to-size grid for inserting a spreadsheet

title: More reliable spreadsheet editing
summary: Formulas, fill-drag, undo and cell formatting behave more predictably, in both the inline editor and the popup.
details: Fill-drag keeps $ absolute references fixed, for example =B3*$C$1/50.
Undo in a spreadsheet only undoes spreadsheet edits, and undo in the text leaves tables alone.
Tab and Enter move between cells, and selected cells and fill-drag are clearly highlighted.
Fixed cell formatting in the popup and a case where saving could blank cells.
imageAlt: Spreadsheet with a highlighted selection and fill handle

title: Project management is now Boards, with richer cards
summary: Tasks are now cards, with status badges, deadlines, linked experiments and resources, and bulk actions.
details: Cards show each linked experiment or resource with its status colour.
Select several cards to archive or delete them together.
Steps and comments can be collapsed, and deadlines show how urgent they are.
Duplicate a card into another project, and open a card straight into edit mode.
imageAlt: A Boards card with status badges and linked items

title: Smoother ordering
summary: Attachments can be reused, orders can advance and archive themselves, and notes support lists.
details: Reuse an attachment across orders, and download it with its own button.
Orders can move from requested to ordered when a procurement ID appears, and archive after a set time.
Notes support bulleted and numbered lists, and long titles and file names wrap properly.

title: A tidier top bar
summary: The navigation bar keeps the key icons visible and folds the rest into a More menu.
details: A Links dropdown groups shortcuts.
The LabCollector link keeps its URL editable from the Tools menu.
imageAlt: The top navigation bar with the More menu open

title: Better notifications and feedback
summary: You are told when someone gives you access, and the Feedback board can sort by votes or date.
details: Notifications arrive when you gain read access to an experiment or resource, even if you had access before.
The dashboard announcement feed is easier to read.
imageAlt: A notification about newly shared access
